prompt: For the week from 3 to 9 March 2025, compare the two competitors' lowest prices. observed_ts holds UTC time: a check counts when its UTC date is in that week. Return three columns, in this order: product_id, bliksem_min_eur and stroomhuis_min_eur, the lowest price_eur each competitor recorded for the product that week, missing when that competitor did not check the product. Return one row for each product checked by at least one of the two competitors that week. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per product checked by either competitor that week

hints: Next, join the two competitors' lists so that a product checked by only one of them keeps its row.
An inner join keeps only products both checked, and a LEFT JOIN keeps one side; the join you need keeps unmatched rows from both lists.
faded_shape:
WITH b AS (SELECT product_id, MIN(price_eur) AS bliksem_min_eur FROM competitor_prices WHERE competitor = 'Bliksem' AND observed_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-03' AND observed_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-10' GROUP BY product_id),
s AS (SELECT product_id, MIN(price_eur) AS stroomhuis_min_eur FROM competitor_prices WHERE competitor = 'Stroomhuis' AND observed_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-03' AND observed_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-10' GROUP BY product_id)
SELECT COALESCE(b.product_id, s.product_id) AS product_id, b.bliksem_min_eur, s.stroomhuis_min_eur
FROM b
why_this_works: FULL OUTER JOIN keeps the products of both lists, matched or not, and COALESCE takes the product_id from whichever side has it.
